newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach down again on regulatory fears.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach down again on regulatory fears.

text.p: Shares in Stagecoach Holdings Plc tumbled for a second day on Thursday, hitting a three-month low amid further worries about a regulatory squeeze on its rail operations, dealers said.

After the stock's 34-1/2p drop on Wednesday, a report in the Financial Times said there was speculation that the industry regulator may force a disposal following problems with the company's South West Trains unit.
"That sort of talk doesn't help," said one market-maker in the stock.
The stock was down 49p at 640 by 1047 GMT in modest volume of 296,931 shares, after hitting a low of 635p -- its lowest since early last December.
Dealers pointed out there was scope for profit-taking in a stock which doubled in value from last July to hit a record 804p on January 21.

With the ruling Conservative party some 20 points behind in the opinion polls ahead of the UK election on May 1, there is talk that an incoming Labour party administration will take a tougher line with privatised companies generally.
Stagecoach has run into particular criticism after train driver redundancies forced it to cancel a number of services on its South West Trains operation.
Rail regulator Opraf, which has imposed fines on SWT for poor performance, last week set new targets for the company and is expected to review progress in April.
If SWT runs fewer than 97.5 percent of scheduled services it faces a possible loss of franchise, though SWT chairman Brian Cox told Reuters last Friday he was confident of avoiding the penalties.
"We should be able to get services running again by Easter," he said, in time to avoid being penalised.
No-one at Stagecoach was available for further comment.
